# Browser QA: Test, Score, Fix, Verify

Test a web app like a real user: click everything, fill every form, check every state. Document every issue with evidence, score the app's health, and end with a ship verdict. In `--fix` mode, also fix bugs in source with one atomic commit per fix and re-verify each one.

## When to Use

- After deploying a feature to staging or preview
- On a feature branch, to verify the branch works (diff-aware mode)
- When you need to verify UI behavior across pages
- Before shipping: confirm layouts, forms, interactions actually work
- When reviewing PRs that touch frontend code
- Accessibility audits and responsive testing
- When the user says a feature is ready for testing, or asks "does this work?"

Never refuse to use the browser once this skill is invoked. Even if the diff has no UI changes, backend changes affect app behavior: open the browser and test. Do not substitute unit tests or evals.

## Tooling (MCP-agnostic)

Use whichever browser automation is available. The phases below are tool-neutral.

- `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` (preferred when present: uses your actual Chrome and its sessions)
- Playwright via an MCP (for example `mcp__playwright__*` or `mcp__browserbase__*`), or a local Playwright script
- Direct Puppeteer scripts
- Optional: the third-party gstack `browse` CLI, if the user has installed it. It adds annotated snapshots (`snapshot -i -a -o <png>`), snapshot diffs after an action (`snapshot -D`), clickable-div discovery (`snapshot -C`), and `console --errors`. Never install it from this skill.

Every screenshot you take, show it to the user (Read the image file) so the evidence is visible.

## Safety first: blast radius (read-only by default)

Browser QA drives real auth and real user journeys, so treat the blast radius explicitly.
Default to **read-only**: never run a **mutating** journey (checkout, payment, delete,
mass-update) against a production URL: require an explicit opt-in **and** a staging or preview
URL. Use seeded **test credentials**, never real production logins, and **redact**
credentials, tokens, and PII before saving any screenshot. Write `[REDACTED]` for passwords in repro steps.

If 2FA or OTP is required, ask the user for the code and wait. If a CAPTCHA blocks you, ask the user to complete it in the browser, then continue.

## Setup

Parse the request:

| Parameter | Default | Override example |
|-----------|---------|-----------------|
| Target URL | auto-detect, or required | `https://staging.example.com`, `http://localhost:3000` |
| Tier | Standard | `--quick`, `--exhaustive` |
| Mode | report-only | `--fix` (test, fix, verify loop) |
| Baseline | none | `--regression .neva/qa-reports/baseline.json` |
| Output dir | `.neva/qa-reports/` | `Output to /tmp/qa` |
| Scope | full app, or diff-scoped on a branch | `Focus on the billing page` |
| Auth | none | test account, or an exported cookie file |

**Tiers decide which issues get fixed in `--fix` mode** (report-only mode documents all of them):
- **Quick:** fix critical + high only
- **Standard:** + medium (default)
- **Exhaustive:** + low and cosmetic

```bash
mkdir -p .neva/qa-reports/screenshots
```

Copy `references/qa-report-template.md` into the output dir as the report skeleton. Start a timer.

## Modes

### Diff-aware (automatic on a feature branch with no URL)

1. Read the branch diff:
   ```bash
   git diff main...HEAD --name-only
   git log main..HEAD --oneline
   ```
2. Map changed files to pages: routes and controllers to URL paths, views and components to the pages that render them, models and services to the pages that use them, CSS to the pages that include it, API endpoints tested directly with a `fetch` from the page.
3. If no page maps from the diff, do not skip browser testing: fall back to Quick (homepage plus top 5 nav targets, console, interactive elements).
4. Find the running app: try `http://localhost:3000`, `:4000`, `:8080`; else a staging or preview URL from the PR or environment; else ask the user.
5. Test each affected page: navigate, screenshot, console, and exercise any changed interaction end to end, capturing before and after.
6. Cross-check commit messages and the PR description for intent, and `TODOS.md` for known bugs on the changed files.
7. Report scoped to the branch: pages tested, does each work (screenshot evidence), any regressions on adjacent pages.

### Full (default when a URL is given)
Visit every reachable page. Document 5 to 10 well-evidenced issues. Produce a health score. Takes 5 to 15 minutes depending on app size.

### Quick (`--quick`)
30-second smoke: homepage plus top 5 navigation targets. Loads? Console errors? Broken links? Health score, no detailed issue write-ups.

### Regression (`--regression <baseline>`)
Run Full, then diff against `baseline.json`: issues fixed, issues new, score delta. Append a Regression section to the report.

## Phase 1: Smoke Test
```
1. Navigate to target URL
2. Check for console errors (filter noise: analytics, third-party)
3. Verify no 4xx/5xx in network requests
4. Screenshot above-the-fold on desktop + mobile viewport
5. Check Core Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms
   (INP replaced FID in March 2024; thresholds per web.dev)
6. Detect framework (note in report metadata):
   __next or _next/data requests -> Next.js; csrf-token meta -> Rails;
   wp-content in URLs -> WordPress; client-side routing, no reloads -> SPA
7. Map navigation (links, or nav elements for SPAs where links are client-side)
```

## Phase 2: Interaction Test

Per page, run the exploration checklist from `references/issue-taxonomy.md`:

```
1. Visual scan: layout, broken images, alignment
2. Interactive elements: click every nav link, button, control. No dead links, no dead buttons
3. Forms: submit valid data (success state), invalid data (error state), empty, long text, special characters
4. Navigation: all paths in and out, back button, deep links, mobile menu
5. States: empty, loading, error, overflow
6. Console: new JS errors or failed requests after each interaction
7. Auth flow: login -> protected page -> logout (test creds only, never prod); logged-out and role boundaries
8. Critical user journeys (checkout, onboarding, search)
   - read-only by default; only exercise mutating journeys against staging
     with explicit opt-in (see "Safety first" above)
```

Depth judgment: more time on core features (home, dashboard, checkout, search), less on secondary pages (about, terms).

## Phase 3: Visual Regression
```
1. Screenshot key pages at 3 breakpoints (375px, 768px, 1440px)
2. Compare against committed baseline screenshots
   - no baseline: report INCONCLUSIVE, never a silent PASS
3. Flag layout shifts > 5px, missing elements, overflow
4. Check dark mode if applicable
```

## Phase 4: Accessibility
```
1. Run axe-core or equivalent on each page
2. Flag WCAG 2.2 AA violations (contrast, labels, focus order)
3. Verify keyboard navigation works end-to-end
4. Check screen reader landmarks
```

> axe-core automatically covers roughly 30 to 40% of WCAG. A clean run is **necessary,
> not sufficient**: keyboard nav, focus order, and a screen-reader pass still need a manual
> check. Do not report "accessible" from an automated pass alone.

## Phase 5: Document (as you go)

Write each issue to the report **immediately when found**. Do not batch.

Before documenting, retry the issue once to confirm it reproduces. Every issue needs at least one screenshot.

- **Interactive bugs** (broken flows, dead buttons, form failures): screenshot before the action, perform it, screenshot the result, capture what changed, write repro steps referencing the screenshots (`issue-001-step-1.png`, `issue-001-result.png`).
- **Static bugs** (typos, layout, missing images): one screenshot showing the problem plus a description.

Severity and category come from `references/issue-taxonomy.md`: critical (blocks a core workflow, data loss, crash), high (major feature broken, no workaround), medium (works with noticeable problems, workaround exists), low (cosmetic).

Depth over breadth: 5 to 10 well-evidenced issues beat 20 vague ones. In report-only mode, test as a user: do not read source code and do not suggest fixes.

## Phase 6: Health Score

Score each category 0 to 100, then take the weighted average.

- **Console (15%)**: 0 errors 100; 1 to 3 errors 70; 4 to 10 errors 40; more than 10 errors 10.
- **Links (10%)**: 0 broken 100; each broken link -15 (minimum 0).
- **Visual, Functional, UX, Content, Performance, Accessibility**: start at 100, per finding deduct critical -25, high -15, medium -8, low -3 (minimum 0).

| Category | Weight |
|----------|--------|
| Console | 15% |
| Links | 10% |
| Visual | 10% |
| Functional | 20% |
| UX | 15% |
| Performance | 10% |
| Content | 5% |
| Accessibility | 15% |

`score = sum(category_score x weight)`

Wrap up: compute the score, write "Top 3 Things to Fix", aggregate console errors, fill severity counts and metadata (date, duration, pages, screenshots, framework), and save `baseline.json`:

```json
{
  "date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "url": "<target>",
  "healthScore": 0,
  "issues": [{ "id": "ISSUE-001", "title": "...", "severity": "...", "category": "..." }],
  "categoryScores": { "console": 0, "links": 0 }
}
```

This is the baseline health score for `--fix` mode.

## Phase 7: Fix Loop (`--fix` only)

Preconditions:
- **Clean working tree.** Run `git status --porcelain`. If non-empty, STOP and ask: commit current changes, stash them (pop after QA), or abort. Each fix needs its own atomic commit.
- Triage: sort issues by severity, fix per tier, mark the rest `deferred`. Issues not fixable from source (third-party widgets, infrastructure) are `deferred` regardless of tier.

For each fixable issue, in severity order:

1. **Locate source.** Grep for error messages, component names, route definitions. Only modify files directly related to the issue.
2. **Fix.** Read the context. Make the minimal fix. No refactors, no features, no unrelated "improvements".
3. **Commit.** One commit per fix, never bundled:
   ```bash
   git add <only-changed-files>
   git commit -m "fix(qa): ISSUE-NNN: short description"
   ```
4. **Re-test.** Navigate back, take a before/after screenshot pair, check the console, confirm the change had the expected effect.
5. **Classify.** `verified` (re-test confirms, no new errors), `best-effort` (applied, could not fully verify, for example needs external service), `reverted` (regression detected: `git revert HEAD`, mark `deferred`).
6. **Regression test** (skip if not `verified`, if the fix is pure CSS, or if no test framework exists and the user declined to add one):
   - Read 2 to 3 nearby tests and match naming, imports, assertion style, setup and teardown exactly.
   - Trace the bug: the precondition that triggered it, the codepath, the exact failing line, adjacent inputs that hit the same path.
   - The test sets up the precondition, performs the action, and asserts the correct behavior (not "it renders" or "it doesn't throw"). Cover adjacent edge cases found while tracing.
   - Test type: console error or logic bug -> unit or integration; broken form or API -> integration with request and response; visual bug with JS behavior -> component test; pure CSS -> skip.
   - Name `{name}.regression-N.test.{ext}` with N = max existing + 1. Add a header comment: `Regression: ISSUE-NNN, {what broke}. Found by browser-qa on {YYYY-MM-DD}.`
   - Run only the new file. Passes: commit `test(qa): regression test for ISSUE-NNN`. Fails: fix the test once; still failing: delete it and defer. More than 2 minutes of exploration: skip and defer.
   - Never modify existing tests or CI configuration; only create new test files.
7. **Self-regulate.** Every 5 fixes, and after any revert, compute:
   ```
   WTF-LIKELIHOOD:
     Start at 0%
     Each revert:                +15%
     Each fix touching >3 files: +5%
     After fix 15:               +1% per additional fix
     All remaining Low severity: +10%
     Touching unrelated files:   +20%
   (test-only commits do not count)
   ```
   **WTF > 20%: STOP.** Show what was done and ask whether to continue. **Hard cap: 50 fixes.**

Then re-run QA on every affected page and compute the final health score. **If the final score is worse than the baseline, warn prominently: something regressed.**

If the repo has a `TODOS.md`: add new deferred bugs with severity, category, and repro steps; annotate fixed ones with the branch and date.

## Output Format

Full report: `.neva/qa-reports/qa-report-{domain}-{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` from `references/qa-report-template.md`, screenshots under `screenshots/`, `baseline.json` alongside. Never delete earlier reports or screenshots.

Summary shape:

```markdown
## QA Report - [URL] - [timestamp]

Health score: 82/100 (baseline 64, delta +18)

### Smoke Test
- Console errors: 0 critical, 2 warnings (analytics noise)
- Network: all 200/304, no failures
- Core Web Vitals: LCP 1.2s PASS, CLS 0.02 PASS, INP 89ms PASS

### Interactions
- [PASS] Nav links: 12/12 working
- [FAIL] ISSUE-001 (high) Contact form: missing error state for invalid email
- [PASS] Auth flow: login/logout working

### Visual
- [FAIL] ISSUE-002 (medium) Hero section overflows on 375px viewport
- [PASS] Dark mode: all pages consistent

### Accessibility
- 2 AA violations: missing alt text on hero image, low contrast on footer links

### Fixes (--fix only)
- verified: 2, best-effort: 0, reverted: 0, deferred: 1

### Verdict: SHIP WITH FIXES (2 issues, 0 blockers)
# verdict: SHIP / SHIP WITH FIXES / DO NOT SHIP; use INCONCLUSIVE if no visual baseline
```

PR one-liner: "QA found N issues, fixed M, health score X -> Y."

Any open critical issue means DO NOT SHIP.

## Framework-Specific Checks

- **Next.js**: hydration errors in console (`Hydration failed`, `Text content did not match`); 404s on `_next/data`; test client-side navigation by clicking, not only direct loads; CLS on dynamic pages.
- **Rails**: N+1 warnings in dev console; CSRF token present in forms; Turbo and Stimulus transitions; flash messages appear and dismiss.
- **WordPress**: plugin JS conflicts; admin bar for logged-in users; `/wp-json/` endpoints; mixed-content warnings.
- **SPA (React, Vue, Angular)**: find nav via the accessibility tree, not links; stale state after navigating away and back; browser back and forward; console growth over extended use.

## Integration

- Pair with `neva-ops:canary-watch` for post-deploy monitoring.
- Pair with `neva-core:benchmark` for performance baselines.
- Fixes in `--fix` mode follow `neva-core:tdd-workflow` for the regression test and `neva-core:verification-loop` before any "fixed" claim.
